chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurara ibn A'yan. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has prescribed upon the people from one Friday to the next thirty-five prayers, among which is one prayer that God prescribed to be performed in congregation — and that is the Friday prayer — and He has exempted it from nine: the child, the elderly, the insane, the traveller, the slave, women, the ill, the blind, and whoever is at the distance of two parasangs.

key_terms.الجمعة: The Friday prayer (Salat al-Jumu'a) — obligatory congregational prayer on Fridays replacing the noon prayer
key_terms.فرسخين: Two parasangs (farsakh) — a unit of distance approximately 5.5 km each, totaling ~11 km as the exemption threshold
key_terms.فرض: Religious obligation, prescribed duty — the strongest level of Islamic legal obligation
key_terms.وضعها: Lifted/exempted — the obligation is removed from certain categories

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from Friday prayer in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) enumerates a key legal ruling on the Friday prayer: Allah has obligated 35 prayers in a week, of which the Friday prayer is the sole prayer specifically mandated to be performed in congregation. However, this congregational obligation is lifted from nine categories of people — children, the elderly, the insane, travelers, slaves, women, the ill, the blind, and those residing two parasangs (approximately 11 km) or more away. This hadith, transmitted through the authoritative chain from Shaykh Saduq through Zurara ibn A'yan, establishes the foundation of Shia fiqh on the conditions and exemptions of Jumu'a prayer.
